FN-BC-001 establishes the claims submission standards — accurate, timely, compliant Medicare billing — an exact match to the Corridor billing row. The CoP citations (42 CFR §484.40, §484.45) confirm direct regulatory alignment. Evidence: P, D, I.

summary: Defines the process for identifying, reporting, and refunding overpayments within the CMS 60-day repayment requirement.

justification: The CMS 60-day overpayment repayment rule (42 CFR §401.305, ACA §6402) requires Medicare providers to identify, report, and refund overpayments within 60 days of identification. Corridor row 2-041 'Corporate Compliance Plan' (HH5-1A) governs the corporate compliance program under which overpayment obligations operate — the compliance program is the organizational mechanism for fulfilling this regulatory obligation. DIRECT because the 60-day overpayment obligation is an explicit federal law requirement that the compliance program must implement. Note: cross-domain overlap with CO-FW-001 (FWA prevention) — both under the compliance program umbrella; FN-BC-004 is the operational billing layer, CO-FW-001 is the program governance layer.

summary: Defines procedures for complying with CMS Pre-Claim Review demonstration programs when applicable.

PCR affirmation records with submission timelines
PCR denial and resubmission records
PCR applicability determination records by payer and geography
justification: Corridor Section 3 billing row is the structural parent for Medicare billing compliance including pre-authorization requirements. FN-BC-005 governs compliance with CMS Pre-Claim Review (PCR), a demonstration program piloted in certain states that requires prior affirmation before Medicare payment. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence because the Corridor's billing row covers general claims submission, but PCR is a CMS demonstration program that applies conditionally by geography and time period — not a standing regulatory requirement with a permanent Corridor row. The PCR requirement post-dates the Corridor's general billing framework and is jurisdictionally variable.

summary: Defines procedures for RAP submission, monitoring, and reconciliation per current CMS payment rules.

RAP (Request for Anticipated Payment) was a CMS Medicare home health billing mechanism that allowed initial payment before episode completion. Under PDGM (effective January 2020), RAPs transitioned to a modified form and were eventually replaced. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence: the Corridor's billing row is the correct parent, but RAP management as a specific billing mechanism — particularly in its PDGM-era modified form — represents a post-Corridor payment model operational requirement that may have no dedicated Corridor row.

The Corridor's billing row covers claims accuracy generally, but PDGM-specific classification requirements — clinical grouping, functional impairment level scoring, comorbidity adjustment, and HIPPS code accuracy — are post-2019 CMS payment model specifics that likely have no dedicated Corridor crosswalk row. PARTIAL because the billing accuracy obligation is established in the Corridor, but PDGM classification governance is a Modern Regulatory Requirement (new payment model) that extends beyond the Corridor's pre-PDGM billing framework.

summary: Defines documentation requirements to support medical necessity for all services billed to Medicare and other payers.
corridorPolicyTitle: Billing and Claims Submission; Contents of Clinical Record

Physician order and certification records demonstrating medical necessity
OASIS assessment records supporting skilled care needs
Clinical documentation audits confirming medical necessity support
justification: Medical necessity documentation is a core Medicare CoP requirement: services billed to Medicare must be supported by clinical documentation demonstrating medical necessity. Corridor Section 3 billing row requires accurate, compliant claims submission (which requires medical necessity support), and row 4-047 'Contents of Clinical Record' requires that clinical records document the necessity of care provided. FN-CM-003's scope — documentation requirements supporting medical necessity for all billed services — directly implements both Corridor rows. Evidence: P, D, I.

justification: Corridor Section 3 billing row covers claims submission compliance, under which episode certification and authorization management operates. summary: Defines monitoring and intervention protocols to minimize Low Utilization Payment Adjustments through visit management.
justification: LUPA (Low Utilization Payment Adjustment) is a PDGM payment model concept introduced in 2020: when a home health episode period falls below the minimum visit threshold for the clinical grouping, the payment is reduced to a per-visit rate. LUPA prevention and monitoring is a pure revenue cycle operational function specific to the PDGM payment model. No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs LUPA thresholds, visit volume monitoring, or PDGM payment adjustment prevention — this concept did not exist in any regulatory framework prior to PDGM's 2020 implementation. Modern Regulatory Requirement — Post-Corridor PDGM Payment Model Layer.

summary: Defines procurement standards, cost controls, and inventory management for medical supplies and equipment.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs supply and equipment cost management from a financial perspective. The OP domain (OP-SL-004) governs equipment and supply management from the clinical operations perspective (procurement, maintenance, calibration). FN-FP-006 governs the same subject from the financial cost control perspective — cost management, inventory valuation, procurement cost controls. This represents a DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_FAMILY with OP-SL-004 across domains: same physical assets, different governance layers (operations vs. finance). Neither the OP nor FN perspective maps to a specific Corridor row for equipment cost governance.
